guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: Bronchodilators for Asthma With Shortness of Breath
recommendation_text: First aid providers should assist a person with asthma who is having difficulty breathing with the administration of their own prescribed bronchodilators as needed.
intervention: Assist with administration of prescribed bronchodilators
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: Bronchodilators for Asthma With Shortness of Breath
recommendation_text: It is reasonable to use either an inhaler with a spacer or a nebulizer when assisting a person with asthma to use their own inhaled bronchodilator medication, in preference to using an inhaler alone.
intervention: Use an inhaler with spacer or a nebulizer rather than an inhaler alone
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: Bronchodilators for Asthma With Shortness of Breath
recommendation_text: If a commercially available spacer is not available, it is reasonable to use an improvised spacer when assisting a person who is having an asthma attack to use their own inhaled bronchodilator medication.
intervention: Use an improvised spacer
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: First Aid for Chemical Exposure to the Eye
recommendation_text: Decontamination by irrigation should be performed immediately after chemical exposure to the eyes.
intervention: Perform immediate irrigation
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: First Aid for Chemical Exposure to the Eye
recommendation_text: Unless otherwise recommended by local guidelines, irrigation with a copious amount of tap water for 15 minutes should be performed.
intervention: Irrigate with copious tap water for 15 minutes
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: First Aid for Chemical Exposure to the Eye
recommendation_text: When providing first aid for chemical eye injury, first aid providers should avoid contaminating other individuals, areas, or the other eye with the caustic substance.
population: Person with chemical eye injury and first aid providers
situation: During first aid for chemical eye injury
intervention: Avoid cross-contamination
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: First Aid for Chemical Exposure to the Eye
recommendation_text: Eye irrigation with normal saline, Ringer's lactate solution, or a commercial eye wash solution if immediately available is reasonable.
situation: An alternative irrigation solution is immediately available
intervention: Use saline, Ringer's lactate, or commercial eye wash
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2024 AHA and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
topic: First Aid for Chemical Exposure to the Eye
recommendation_text: It is reasonable for individuals with ocular exposure to industrial chemicals to adhere to local guidelines or recommendations from a poison center.
population: Individuals with industrial chemical eye exposure
intervention: Follow local guidelines or poison center recommendations
verification_notes: Checked against 2024 AHA First Aid guideline recommendation table; recommendation wording, COR and LOE match.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Recognition of Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: If an adult is unconscious/unresponsive, with absent or abnormal breathing (ie, only gasping), the lay rescuer should assume the person is in cardiac arrest.
situation: Absent or abnormal breathing, including gasping
intervention: Lay rescuer should assume cardiac arrest
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 8 (printed page S455); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Recognition of Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: If an adult is unconscious/unresponsive, with absent or abnormal breathing (ie, only gasping), the health care professional should check for a pulse for no more than 10 s and, if no definite pulse is felt, should assume the person is in cardiac arrest.
intervention: Healthcare professional checks pulse for no more than 10 seconds
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 8 (printed page S455); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Lay Rescuer
recommendation_text: All lay rescuers should provide chest compressions for adults with presumed cardiac arrest.
intervention: Provide chest compressions
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 9 (printed page S456); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Lay Rescuer
recommendation_text: After identifying an adult in cardiac arrest, a lone responder should activate the emergency response system first, then immediately begin CPR, beginning with chest compressions.
intervention: Activate emergency response system, then begin CPR with chest compressions
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 9 (printed page S456); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Lay Rescuer
recommendation_text: For adults in cardiac arrest, a lone rescuer with a mobile phone should activate the emergency response system and immediately begin CPR, beginning with chest compressions.
situation: Lone rescuer has a mobile phone
intervention: Activate emergency response system and begin CPR with chest compressions
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 9 (printed page S456); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Lay Rescuer
recommendation_text: For lay rescuers trained in performing CPR, it is reasonable to provide ventilation (breaths) in addition to chest compressions for an adult in cardiac arrest.
situation: Lay rescuer is trained in CPR
intervention: Provide ventilation in addition to chest compressions
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 9 (printed page S456); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Lay Rescuer
recommendation_text: When immediately available, it is reasonable for rescuers to use PPE during CPR for adult cardiac arrest.
population: Rescuers and adults in cardiac arrest
situation: PPE is immediately available during CPR
intervention: Use personal protective equipment
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 9 (printed page S456); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Health Care Professional
recommendation_text: During adult cardiac arrest, a lone health care professional should commence with chest compressions rather than with ventilation.
intervention: Commence with chest compressions rather than ventilation
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 10 (printed page S457); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Initiation of Resuscitation: Health Care Professional
recommendation_text: It is reasonable for health care professionals to perform chest compressions and ventilation for all adult patients in cardiac arrest from either a cardiac or noncardiac cause.
intervention: Perform chest compressions and ventilation
verification_notes: Checked against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 10 (printed page S457); recommendation wording, COR and LOE match. PDF page corrected where needed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway After Head and Neck Trauma
recommendation_text: In cases of head and neck trauma, trained rescuers should open the airway of an adult by using a jaw thrust without head extension.
population: Trained rescuers assisting adults with head and neck trauma
situation: Airway management after head and neck trauma
intervention: Open airway using jaw thrust without head extension
verification_notes: Visually verified against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 12, printed page S459. Recommendation text, COR 1 and LOE C-EO confirmed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway After Head and Neck Trauma
recommendation_text: For an adult with head and neck trauma, if the airway cannot be opened with a jaw thrust and airway adjunct insertion, trained rescuers should open the airway by using a head tilt–chin lift.
population: Trained rescuers assisting adults with head and neck trauma
situation: Airway cannot be opened using jaw thrust and airway adjunct insertion
intervention: Open airway using head tilt–chin lift
verification_notes: Visually verified against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 12, printed page S459. Recommendation text, COR 1 and LOE C-EO confirmed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway After Head and Neck Trauma
recommendation_text: In the setting of an adult with head and neck trauma, lay rescuers should not use rigid cervical devices for spinal motion restriction because their use by untrained rescuers may be harmful.
population: Lay rescuers assisting adults with head and neck trauma
intervention: Avoid rigid cervical devices for spinal motion restriction
verification_notes: Visually verified against 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 12, printed page S459. Recommendation text, COR 3: Harm and LOE C-LD confirmed.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: In adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees whenever possible.
intervention: Position the patient's torso approximately at the rescuer's knee level
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: When providing chest compressions for an adult, the rescuer should place the heel of one hand on the center (middle) of the person's chest (the lower half to lower third of the sternum) and the heel of the other hand on top of the first so that the hands are overlapped.
intervention: Place overlapping hands on the center of the chest
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: In adult cardiac arrest, resuscitation should generally be conducted where the person is found, as long as high-quality CPR can be administered safely and effectively.
intervention: Perform CPR where the person is found when safe and effective
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: In adult cardiac arrest, it is preferred to perform CPR on a firm surface and with the person in the supine position, when feasible and it does not delay chest compressions.
situation: Surface and body positioning for CPR
intervention: Use a firm surface and supine position when feasible
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: In adult cardiac arrest, rescuers may consider placing their dominant hand on the sternum when performing chest compressions.
intervention: Consider placing the dominant hand on the sternum
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Positioning and Location for CPR
recommendation_text: For adult patients who experience cardiac arrest while in the prone position, it may be reasonable to turn the patient supine before initiating chest compressions. If the patient cannot be safely turned supine, rescuers may consider performing CPR in the prone position.
situation: Cardiac arrest occurring in the prone position
intervention: Turn supine before compressions when feasible; consider prone CPR if turning is unsafe
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: In adult cardiac arrest, preshock and postshock pauses in chest compressions should be as short as possible.
intervention: Minimize preshock and postshock compression pauses
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: During rhythm checks for adult cardiac arrest, the health care professional should minimize the time taken to check for a pulse (no more than 10 s), and if the rescuer does not definitely feel a pulse, chest compressions should be restarted immediately.
intervention: Limit pulse checks to 10 seconds and restart compressions if no definite pulse is felt
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: In adults with cardiac arrest, it is reasonable to immediately resume chest compressions after shock administration rather than pause CPR to perform a postshock rhythm check.
intervention: Resume chest compressions immediately after shock administration
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: When 2 or more rescuers are available during an adult cardiac arrest, it is reasonable to switch chest compressors approximately every 2 min (or after about 5 cycles of compressions and ventilation at a ratio of 30:2).
intervention: Rotate chest compressors approximately every two minutes
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: For adults in cardiac arrest receiving CPR without an advanced airway, it is reasonable to pause compressions to deliver 2 breaths, each given over 1 s.
intervention: Pause compressions to deliver two breaths, each over one second
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: During adult cardiac arrest, it may be reasonable to perform CPR with a chest compression fraction of at least 60%.
intervention: Consider maintaining a chest compression fraction of at least 60%
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Fraction and Pauses
recommendation_text: Outside of the advanced life support environment, where invasive monitoring is available, there are insufficient data about the value of a pulse check while performing CPR for adult cardiac arrest.
situation: Pulse checks during CPR outside advanced life support
intervention: Evidence is insufficient to establish the value of pulse checks
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Depth and Rate in Adult Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: During manual CPR, rescuers should perform chest compressions to a depth of at least 2 inches, or 5 cm, for an average adult while avoiding excessive chest compression depths (>2.4 inches, or 6 cm).
situation: Chest compression depth during manual CPR
intervention: Compress at least 2 inches while avoiding depths greater than 2.4 inches
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Depth and Rate in Adult Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: During adult cardiac arrest, it is reasonable to use audiovisual feedback devices for real-time optimization of CPR performance.
intervention: Use audiovisual feedback devices
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Depth and Rate in Adult Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: For adults in cardiac arrest, it is reasonable for rescuers to perform chest compressions at a rate of 100 to 120/min.
intervention: Perform compressions at 100–120 per minute
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Depth and Rate in Adult Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: It can be beneficial for rescuers to allow complete chest wall recoil for adults in cardiac arrest, such as by not leaning on the chest between compressions.
intervention: Allow complete chest wall recoil and avoid leaning
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Chest Compression Depth and Rate in Adult Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: During adult cardiac arrest, it may be reasonable to perform chest compressions so that chest compression and recoil/relaxation times are approximately equal.
intervention: Consider approximately equal compression and recoil times
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE confirmed. PDF pages 13, 15 or 16; printed pages S460, S462 or S463.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway in Adults in Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: For unresponsive adult patients, health care professionals and trained lay rescuers should open the airway by using a head tilt–chin lift maneuver when no cervical spine injury is suspected.
population: Unresponsive adults without suspected cervical spine injury
situation: Opening the airway during adult cardiac arrest
intervention: Use a head tilt–chin lift maneuver
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 11, printed page S458. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE checked against the source table.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway in Adults in Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: When managing the airway of an adult with known or suspected basal skull fracture or severe coagulopathy, an oropharyngeal airway is preferred compared with a nasopharyngeal airway.
population: Adults with known or suspected basal skull fracture or severe coagulopathy
intervention: Prefer an oropharyngeal airway over a nasopharyngeal airway
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 11, printed page S458. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE checked against the source table.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway in Adults in Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: The use of an airway adjunct (eg, oropharyngeal or nasopharyngeal airway) may be reasonable in unconscious adult patients with no cough or gag reflex to facilitate delivery of ventilation.
population: Unconscious adults without cough or gag reflex
intervention: Consider use of an oropharyngeal or nasopharyngeal airway adjunct
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 11, printed page S458. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE checked against the source table.

guideline_title: 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC
topic: Opening the Airway in Adults in Cardiac Arrest
recommendation_text: The routine use of cricoid pressure in adult cardiac arrest is not recommended.
intervention: Do not routinely use cricoid pressure
verification_notes: Visually verified against the original 2025 AHA Adult BLS guideline, PDF page 11, printed page S458. Recommendation wording, COR and LOE checked against the source table.
